The *Maṭṭhakuṇḍalīvimānavatthu* (Vv 83) is a canonical verse narrative belonging to the *Vimānavatthu* collection. The text recounts how a deva appears to his grieving father to console him and teach him how to end his sorrow through the Dhamma.

 Automated text-reuse data from DharmaNexus strongly supports these relationships, documenting an identical textual parallel with Pv 17 (§0.4–22.1 ↔ §0.3–22.1) and substantial verse overlap with Ja 449 (§0.3–10.4), as well as shared formulaic verses (notably §7.4–10.4) recurring in Ja 352, Ja 372, Ja 410, and Ja 454 [DharmaNexus]. Substantial portions of the verses are embedded and commented upon within the commentarial tradition, most heavily in the *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Dhammapada-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, and various volumes of the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. In addition, DharmaNexus identifies low-scoring automated cross-language alignments with the Tibetan translation of the *Karmaśataka* [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on catalog and DharmaNexus data.*
